game: ATL@NE Week 9 2025, kickoff 2025-11-02 13:00 ET, Gillette outdoors, NE -5.5, total 45.5

script.base: New England is the book favorite at -5.5 with implied totals NE 25.5 / ATL 20.0 on a moderate 45.5 total, so the base script is NE in front by a score by the second half, closing with the run after Rhamondre Stevenson (45 carries, 140 yards in weeks 6-8) is out. Drake Maye does not need a shootout. Atlanta, as the dog, falls behind and throws more to Drake London (26 targets, 282 air yards L3) and Kyle Pitts (23 targets) than it grinds Tyler Allgeier.
script.flip1: Atlanta hangs within a field goal or leads: Penix stays balanced, Bijan Robinson keeps a 14-18 carry load (he had 42 carries / 235 rush yards in weeks 6-8), and New England has to throw, which lifts Kayshon Boutte / Stefon Diggs and cuts Henderson's late-carry script.
script.flip2: New England jumps ahead by 17+: Atlanta abandons the run (Bijan rush yards die, London/Pitts get garbage targets) and Henderson's starter snaps get cut in the fourth, so a big NE rushing day can stall even if the early script was right.

injury_fallout: Official pre-game report, not final inactives (~90 min pre-kick not in pack). NE RB Rhamondre Stevenson Out (Toe): weeks 6-8 he had 45 carries / 140 yards, the clear lead share. Next man up on the L3 rush log is TreVeyon Henderson (21/107, 5.1 YPC), not Antonio Gibson (absent from the weeks 6-8 rusher list; Terrell Jennings only 7/33). Drake Maye also ran 18/147 in that window, so vacated carries can leak to the QB. ATL T Storm Norton Out (Foot) raises pressure risk and lowers ATL rushing efficiency, which points to more quick throws (Bijan/Pitts catches up, deep WR yards down). ATL WR Casey Washington Out (Back) shifts a small target slice (5 targets / 42 yards L3) toward London, Pitts, Darnell Mooney and K.Hodge. ATL DT Zach Harrison Out (Knee) and LB Jalon Walker Questionable (Groin) weaken an already soft run front. ATL CB Billy Bowman Jr. Out (Hamstring) and S Jessie Bates Questionable (Knee) are coverage holes for NE pass-catchers, but no charting maps who they covered. ATL LB Leonard Floyd Questionable (Hamstring) is an edge-rush question mark for NE pass pro. Sources: pack injury report and weeks 6-8 usage; final inactives unknown.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Team location splits only: NE defense YPA left 7.56 (106), middle 7.46 (59), right 7.93 (85), fairly even. ATL defense YPA left 5.86 (63), middle 10.61 (36), right 4.67 (83) — the bleed is the middle, not the outside.
matchup.pressure: NE blitz rate 23% (low). ATL EPA/db is -0.25 when blitzed vs +0.05 vs no blitz, so Penix is fine in base and worse under pressure. ATL blitz rate 44%. NE EPA/db is +0.47 vs blitz and +0.26 vs none, so Maye beats Atlanta's pressure look. No time-to-throw or sack rates saved. Norton Out is the ATL pass-pro risk even against a low-blitz NE front.
matchup.bleeds: NE run defense is the strength: 3.62 YPC allowed, only 12 runs of 10+ in 8 games. NE pass defense bleeds explosives: 28 passes of 20+ for 269 yards. ATL run defense bleeds: 4.68 YPC and 23 runs of 10+ in 7 games, worse with Harrison Out. ATL does not bleed deep volume (only 11 passes of 20+ for 198 yards in 7 games) but the middle is open at 10.61 YPA.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Henderson's carries into Atlanta's run bleed (4.68 YPC, 23 explosive runs) in a NE-lead script, with Stevenson Out. London's 282 air yards L3 overlap NE's 28 explosive passes allowed, but Norton Out cuts against deep WR yards, so that overlap is not a leg. Boutte's 237 air yards on only 12 targets L3 attack the part of Atlanta's defense that has limited 20+ passes, not the middle bleed. Diggs (15 targets, 79 air L3) is the shorter look that fits the middle, but his line is not a clean number.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Stevenson is out after 45 carries and 140 yards over the last three games, Henderson is already the next man (21 carries, 107 yards, 5.1 YPC in that same window), Atlanta allows 4.68 YPC and 23 runs of 10+, and NE at -5.5 with a 25.5 implied total is the side that runs late, so 27.5 is a complement-role number on a lead-back day.
edge_players.must_be_true: Stevenson stays inactive, Henderson gets the early-down share rather than a Gibson/Maye/Jennings split that leaves him under 8 carries, and the game does not flip to an Atlanta lead that makes NE throw the whole second half.
edge_players.kills_it: Maye's 18 carries / 147 rush yards L3 plus a Gibson revival steal the vacated work, Henderson repeats the 5-yard game in last4, or NE trails and abandons the run before he clears a low bar. A late blowout can also cap snaps after a slow start.

data_check.notes: No projection, no sims, no Pinnacle no-vig, and every main line is 'no price' with a stand-in label whose numeric season median is not in the pack. Henderson over 27.5 is a strong injury/script/matchup read. Data does not fully agree: last4 rush sample 24, 27, 5, 75 has a median under 27.5, while L3 mean 35.7 agrees. Per the rules that disagreement FLAGS the strong read and does not cut it. model_p 0.63 is a hand read, not a 3-sim, and is kept under 70% on purpose. The 3-point edge gate cannot run without no-vig. Second candidates dropped, not flagged: Bijan rush under 72.5 is only a lean and the L3 rush mean 78.3 (170+40+25) disagrees, so the lean is dropped; London rec over 55.5 fights the Norton-Out quick-game rule (deep WR yards down) despite NE allowing 28 passes of 20+; Boutte rec over 49.5 has hot form (L3 223 yards, last4 43/93/55/75) but Atlanta has allowed only 11 passes of 20+ and the favorite script is run-leaning; Pitts 59.5, Diggs 44.5, Henry 36.5, Mooney 20.5, Allgeier 24.5 and Gibson 27.5 are not clean enough to write as an edge. No prices means nothing is sized.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and Henderson under 27.5 lost the ticket because Stevenson' s 15 carries a game did not transfer. Maye kept the designed/scramble run game that produced 147 rush yards in three weeks, Gibson came off the inactive-looking L3 role and took the early downs, and Henderson stayed the change-of-pace who just posted a 5-yard game. Or Atlanta led, NE threw, and the late-carry script never showed up. The 27.5 price may also have already moved and this pack simply has no quote, so the 'unmoved sleeper' part of the read can be wrong even if the role read is right.
slip_story: One-story favorite clock stack: NE -5.5 leads, Stevenson is out, Henderson rush over is the lead-back leg against a 4.68 YPC Atlanta front. No second leg survived the pre-mortem, so this is a single, not a slip. Do not pair it with a game under, with Bijan rush over (opposite trench read), or with NE WR overs that need a pass-heavy NE script.
